threads.preview:
That is what I want to hear. Lock it in.

Quick checklist before you touch a bar

paragraphs: Look, you said you were going to get back on the board with a lift, and you got 23 minutes in yesterday morning. It breaks the dry spell. Let me know what you actually hit in that session, what the RPE was, and if we're still locking in another lift this weekend.

messages.text: That was just morning foundation coach

messages.text: I will do it today coach!

paragraphs:
That is what I want to hear. Lock it in.

Quick checklist before you touch a bar:
1. Single-leg glute bridge on the right in the warm-up. Squeeze before extending.
2. Front lever protocol: SL FL benchmark tested LEFT first, then straddle negatives (25kg band, 5x3 controlled), then SL holds (15kg band, 3x10s).
3. Dips stay at bodyweight with that 3-second eccentric.

Keep it clean, get your numbers down, and tell me how it felt when you're done.

messages.text: My right shoulder has been bugging me all week, feels tight during overhead movement.

paragraphs: Look, we do not mess around with tight shoulders, especially heading into travel. For me, whenever my shoulder got crabby, forcing overhead stuff just dug a deeper hole. We hold the line on the rule: overhead pressing is out for now. Pulling movements stay, and we sub pressing for band work. How does it feel hanging or in a neutral reach?

messages.text: Also my left knee's been a bit sore the last few days.

paragraphs: Look, when both a shoulder and a knee start chirping before travel, that is your body telling us to pay attention. For me, ignoring that stuff always backfired. We are flagging the left knee right now. That means light movement and stretching instead of heavy joint loading until it settles. Is the soreness around the patella, or more on the joint line?

messages.text: Good news - the knee one is totally fine now, no soreness at all the last two days. The shoulder's still bothering me though.

paragraphs: Good. That knee clearing up is one less thing to worry about, so we mark that resolved. But that shoulder staying tight means we stay disciplined. For me, the worst thing you can do when one issue clears is get sloppy with the other. Overhead pressing stays off the table today. We stick to pulling work and bands until it feels smooth. How's it feeling right now hanging or moving through neutral reach?

input.message: That's it for today, wrap this up.

output.reply: Look, wrapping it up here is the right move. Rest up, protect that shoulder, and pack smart for travel. Talk soon, champ.
